title: Fix backlog: consolidated QA and panel findings

rules.dedupe: Findings that describe the same defect (same page and element, or the same root cause and fix) are merged into one item; evidence from every source is kept, with source ids.
rules.severity: Highest source rating; raised one level when three or more independent evaluations found the defect (so high becomes critical); a low raised to medium when two evaluations found it. No evaluator rated anything critical on its own.
rules.priority: P0 = critical or high; or named by at least two of the three panels (findings, ranked weaknesses or must-fix lists); or on the security evaluator's fix-before-production list; or a dependency of a P0 item. P1 = every other in-repo fix. P2 = needs MAHB data or partners; out of scope this round, with the reason.
rules.ownership: Each file has exactly one owning package (longest owned prefix wins). An item lists only files its package owns; changes needed in another package's files are listed as hand-offs.

packages.name: Shell, home, search and design system
packages.scope: Header, navigation, airport chrome, home page, home and site search, shared common and UI components, tokens, fonts and the core English and Malay dictionaries.

findings.title: About 440 px of airport chrome pushes every task answer below the first phone screen
findings.acceptance: On every airport sub-page (board, flight, transport, parking, facilities, map, transit, lounges, shop and dine) at 360x800, 390x664 and 390x844, English and Malay: the airport header collapses to one row of at most 56 px (code, terminal, clock and sections behind one control); the h1 starts at or above 200 px at 100% text and is never under the fixed bottom bar at 125% text; the first board row is inside the first 664 px; the full airport banner remains only on the overview. A Playwright first-screen test asserting these positions runs in CI.
findings.evidence: h1 at 440 px on the flight, transport, parking, facilities, map and transit pages at 390x844 and 390x664 (414 px on the board, 466 px on parking at 360, 516 px on the Malay flight page at 360). Answers: gate 1,306 px, first board row 1,173-1,185 px, KLIA Ekspres fare 1,312-1,500 px, parking quick-stay 2,029 px. The chrome is the concept banner, header, airport banner with clock, three terminal chips, a 9-tab strip and a breadcrumb (usability-06, exec-commerce-08, ux-frequent-07). Strategy principles 1 and 3 require the answer in the first screen at 360x800. First-time-access Q10 #3 asks for the same compact header.
findings.severity_basis: raised from high: found independently by 3 evaluations

findings.title: Header airport switcher fails Label in Name (WCAG 2.5.3, Level A) on every airport page
findings.acceptance: The accessible name begins with the visible text in both languages (for example "KUL T1, change airport (currently KLIA Terminal 1)"), or aria-label is removed in favour of the visible text plus a visually hidden suffix. axe with wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa plus the label-content-name-mismatch rule reports 0 violations on /en/kul, /en/kul/flights, /ms/kul/map and /en/concierge with an airport chosen; this package's specs import the shared tag list from E (CI item).
findings.evidence: Visible text "KUL" (plus the "T1" badge) but aria-label "Change airport. Currently KLIA Terminal 1" (src/components/shell/airport-switcher.tsx:97, src/lib/i18n/en.ts:722). axe label-content-name-mismatch on every airport page in light, dark, both high-contrast themes and 125% text, English and Malay, at 1440, 390 and 360 px; also on /ms/concierge and /en/corporate/news once an airport is chosen; Lighthouse lists it on the board, flight and transport pages. The suite reported 0 violations because AXE_TAGS omit wcag21a (e2e/platform.spec.ts:13, e2e/guides.spec.ts:11).
findings.severity_basis: raised from high: found independently by 3 evaluations
handoffs: B, C, D: replace the local AXE_TAGS constant in e2e/flights.spec.ts, concierge.spec.ts, map.spec.ts, transport.spec.ts, commerce.spec.ts, guides.spec.ts and corporate.spec.ts with the shared list from e2e/support/axe.ts (one line each).

findings.title: The home's main search is flights-only: topic queries dead-end and Enter does nothing
findings.acceptance: In the home and overview search: a query with no flight match shows the top three site-search entities inline plus "See all results for <query>" linking to /<lang>/search?q=; Enter on a single exact flight-number match opens that flight; Enter otherwise opens /<lang>/search?q=<query>; flights stay first when both match; the live-region announcement is kept. e2e covers "parking", "arrival card", "MH2072" and "KUL-PEN" in English and Malay.
findings.evidence: "arrival card", "parking", "lounge" and "fast track" in the home field give "0 flights found" with no route to site search, and Enter stays on /en (usability-03, ux-frequent-05); site search returns 14 parking and 10 lounge results for the same words. Typing "MH2072" and pressing Enter leaves the URL at /ms because onSubmit prevents navigation (src/components/flights/flight-search-box.tsx:162), so nothing visibly happens for a sighted user (first-time-access-17). BR-19 requires one search for flights, facilities, services and pages.
findings.severity_basis: raised from high: found independently by 3 evaluations

findings.title: Demo label out of view on phone board previews and search results; the full demo banner crowds flight first screens
findings.acceptance: A compact demo tag component (one line, at most 24 px, visible text "Demo", accessible name "Demonstration data") exists in src/components/common and is used on every preview row or group header at narrow widths; the in-view check (each demo row scrolled to the viewport centre, visible demo markers counted) reports 100% of rows labelled on /en, /ms, /en/kul and /en/search?q=MH at 390x844 and 1280x900; the full banner appears at most once per page and is no taller than 48 px on flight surfaces; the in-view check runs in CI.
findings.evidence: Phone 390x844: home board preview 6 of 8 rows with no demonstration label in view (/ms the same), /en/kul overview preview 4 of 6, /en/search?q=MH and ?q=AK 4 of 8 flight results; desktop passes (content-integrity-02). Conversely the full striped banner takes about 200 px between the flight h1 and "Flight status" on the phone (usability-18). Build spec rule 1: a demonstration label is visible wherever a flight row, gate or status appears.
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, high; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Focus falls to <body> after following an in-page link; the next Tab jumps to the footer (WCAG 2.4.3)
findings.acceptance: After any client-side navigation that changes the pathname (not the query alone), focus moves to the new page's h1 (tabindex=-1) or main, the route announcer still announces the title, and the next Tab reaches the first interactive element after the h1. An e2e test asserts document.activeElement after the three navigations above.
findings.evidence: Keyboard only at 1280x800: after Enter on a link inside main, document.activeElement is BODY and the first Tab focuses the footer link "Malaysia Airports home" at scrollY 997; reproduced on 3 navigations (home to flight, home to map, guides to journey). Links in persistent navigation keep focus. All three panels list it as open (exec and ux nav scorecards; first-time-access Q10 must-fix #4).

findings.title: Search palette: active option marked only by a 1.03:1 to 1.22:1 tint, and the text field has no focus ring
findings.acceptance: The active option differs from its neighbours by at least 3:1 in light, dark, light HC and dark HC (focus-colour outline or a 4 px inset bar alongside the tint), and the input wrapper shows the standard focus ring; contrast measured by script in all four themes.
findings.evidence: aria-selected background #e7e8f4 on #ffffff = 1.22:1 (light and light high contrast) and #20245a on #1f2350 = 1.03:1 (dark); no outline, bar or icon; DOM focus stays in the combobox (src/components/search/command-palette.tsx:43). The palette combobox has outline none and no wrapper ring, unlike the home and board search fields (WCAG 1.4.11, 2.4.7).

findings.title: Home tiles and navigation silently fall back to the airport overview when a section is missing
findings.acceptance: When hasSection() is false the tile and primary-nav item stay visible but read "<section>: not published for <airport>" and lead to an honest state with the official page and phone (or are hidden with a one-line note); no tile or nav item named after a section lands on the overview; a unit test covers 39 airports x 9 sections.
findings.evidence: After choosing Subang, the home tiles "Getting to the airport", "Parking", "Terminal maps", "Lounges" and "Food and shops" all link to /en/szb, whose overview never mentions parking; szb, kch and lgk return 404 for parking, transport, lounges, shop-dine and facilities. sectionHref() replaces any unavailable section with "overview" without telling the user (src/components/shell/sections.ts).

findings.title: The home page ignores the visitor's saved flight
findings.acceptance: With a saved flight for today or later, /en and /ms show that flight's live card (status, terminal, gate, next timeline step, arrive-by) above the journey modes in the first phone screen at 390x844, with 0 interactions; with none saved the sample teaser shows as now; the server HTML reserves the card's height so CLS on /en stays at or under 0.05 after hydration.
findings.evidence: After saving MH 2630 (localStorage ma:journey:v1 holds it and /en/journey lists it), "MH 2630" appears nowhere in /en main: the teaser still says "Save a flight and we build a timeline" with a sample flight ("Be at the airport by 17:30") and the board preview stays network-wide; only the tab-bar Journey badge shows "1". journey-teaser.tsx always picks a sample flight from the demo provider.

findings.title: Home hydration blocks the main thread for 1.4 to 2.0 s; early taps are lost and switcher and mode taps exceed 200 ms
findings.acceptance: On a 4x-throttled mobile profile: /en and /ms TBT at or under 200 ms (median of 3 Lighthouse runs); no flight pool is built during render (built lazily on first focus or keystroke inside startTransition, or served from the server); the journey-mode switch, airport-switcher open and close (home and /en/kul) and the journey direction switch each respond within 200 ms (Event Timing, 3 runs); 6 of 6 taps made 0 to 600 ms after DOMContentLoaded take effect.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse mobile TBT 1,391 ms (/en) and 1,978 ms (/ms), longest task 1,202 and 1,419 ms; 653 ms self time in zonedParts (src/lib/time.ts) called by DemoFlightProvider during React render because the home search box builds a pool for every demo airport before anyone types. After hydration at 4x CPU: journey-mode switch 392-520 ms, home airport switcher open 320-408 ms, /en/kul switcher 224-304 ms, /en/journey direction switch 208-216 ms. Taps 300-600 ms after DOMContentLoaded took 1,280-1,472 ms and 3 of 6 earlier taps did not change the radio (performance-03, performance-14). First-time-access measured /ms TBT 1,434 ms and a 0.158 shift on a throttled mid-range profile (first-time-access-11; the shift is tracked under the font item).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, high; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Display font not preloaded: the Malay h1 rewraps (CLS 0.16) and home fonts weigh 206 KB
findings.acceptance: CLS at or under 0.05 on /ms and /en, mobile and desktop, in 3 runs with fonts loading normally and with Fraunces blocked; Fraunces upright preloaded on pages whose h1 uses it; fallback metrics (size-adjust, ascent-override) tuned so the Malay h1 wraps the same in both faces; the italic file dropped or subset to the glyphs used; home fonts at or under 150 KB; Geist Mono loaded only where tabular data is above the fold.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse mobile CLS 0.161 on /ms in 3 of 3 runs; Playwright 0.154-0.158: the search card and the content below move up 27 px (mobile) or 56 px (desktop) at 242-277 ms, right after Fraunces loads; the Malay h1 is 2 lines in the fallback face and 1 line in Fraunces. Fraunces is declared with preload: false (src/fonts/index.ts lines 24 and 45). Home fonts 206 KB against a 150 KB budget (Fraunces 67 KB, Fraunces italic 81 KB for "beautifully connected." only, Geist Mono 24 KB on every page); on congested Wi-Fi Fraunces starts at 2.4 s and LCP is 2.9 s. First-time-access measured the same 0.158 shift (first-time-access-11).

findings.title: Fixed header, bottom bar and floating search button cover content at large text and on the home first screen
findings.acceptance: Below 640 px viewport height or at 112-125% text the header hides on scroll down and returns on scroll up, and the bottom bar collapses; page padding-bottom and scroll-padding equal the bar plus the button overhang, so no fixed element covers text or a tappable target (screenshot check at 360, 390 and 430 px at 100% and 125%); at 320x568 with 125% text fixed chrome takes at most 15% of the viewport while content scrolls.
findings.evidence: 320x256 (400% zoom): sticky header 68 px plus bottom bar 57 px = 125 of 256 px (accessibility-09). 320x568 at 125% text: 85 px plus 71-74 px, 28% of the viewport on every page; at 390 px the round search button overlaps the board intro, the map intro and the accessibility hub's fifth chip (first-time-access-12). On the home first screen at 390 px the raised search button covers the "Lounges" tile label ("Loun...") (ux-frequent-18).
findings.severity_basis: raised from medium: found independently by 3 evaluations

findings.title: Site search vocabulary and ranking: "fast track", "lift", "buggy", "troli" and "tukar wang" return nothing; news outranks facilities
findings.acceptance: A bilingual synonym table (lift/lif/elevator, buggy, troli, pengurup wang/tukar wang, fast track/laluan pantas/priority lane, surau/prayer room, halal) and type boosts that demote news for facility-type queries; map places (lifts, information counters) and airline entities (airline, KLIA terminal, provenance) indexed; an explicit "Not published" result for known unpublished topics (accessible parking, hearing loops); src/lib/search/search.test.ts asserts the first result for at least 15 listed queries, including "fast track" once the Fast Track record exists.
findings.evidence: 0 results for "fast track", "lift", "buggy" (en), "troli" and "tukar wang" (ms); "halal" ranks unrelated help answers above the halal outlet; "hearing loop" returns the inter-terminal shuttle and Kota Kinabalu buses; "accessible parking" ranks Penang standard parking first; "surau" ranks a solar-farm news item second (docs-05, first-time-access-13). "AirAsia" returns flight rows with no airline entity (usability-13, tracked in the concierge item).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations
findings.priority_reason: a P0 item depends on it (B-08)

findings.title: Section tab strips are clipped mid-word with no overflow cue; Malay tab-bar labels crowd
findings.acceptance: At 1280, 1440 and 1920 px all section tabs fit, or overflow is signalled with an edge fade and scroll buttons; no tab label is clipped mid-word at any width from 320 to 1920 px in either language (active tab scrolled into view with inline padding); Malay bottom-bar labels fit on one line with a visible gap at 360 px; screenshot test at 360, 390, 1280 and 1440 px.
findings.evidence: "KLIA sections" nav: scrollWidth 1,347 px in a 1,240 px container at 1280, 1440 and 1920 px; "Connections anc" cut at the right on the flight page and "rview" at the left on shop and dine; overflow-x auto with no mask or buttons. At 360 px in Malay the strip opens scrolled so the first label reads "ran keseluruhan". Bottom-bar labels "Laman utama" and "Penerbangan" run together at 390 px (dark) and wrap at 360 px.
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Provenance chips and micro-labels compete with the answers; tag names are inconsistent
findings.acceptance: One tag set in both languages (Official, Estimated, Suggestion, Demo, Not published) with "instruction" reserved for rules; per-fact sources behind a small marker that opens a popover; unpublished fields grouped into one muted line per card; at most 8 type sizes on any page; mono capitals limited to data labels in the flight card and board; re-running the DOM count script at 390 px shows at least 40% fewer chips on Facilities and Transport than the counts above.
findings.evidence: Phone: Facilities 17.5 screens with about 21 provenance tags, 21 "N sources" toggles and 27 "Not published/not verified" mentions; Transport 13.2 screens with 22 not-verified mentions; Map about 24 tags and 18 demo labels; tag names vary ("Official instruction"/"Official", "Estimated guidance"/"Estimated") and "Official instruction" is applied to facts (usability-17). Home: 78 upper-case micro-labels, 86 monospaced runs, 13 font sizes; Transport 64 upper-case labels (ux-frequent-15). Exec panel Q3: every card carries badges, which "reads as an information system rather than a premium brand".
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations
handoffs: C: adopt the grouped "Not published" line in facility, lounge, outlet and car-park cards.
D: retag content records where "instruction" is used for facts.

findings.title: Assistance is not in the desktop header
findings.acceptance: "Assistance" is a labelled link to /<lang>/accessibility in the desktop header (primary nav or top bar beside Display settings) and in the first group of the phone Menu, in both languages; e2e asserts it at 1280 and 390 px.
findings.evidence: Desktop header: Flights, Plan your journey, At the airport, Shop & dine, Transport & parking, Help, plus icon buttons. /accessibility is linked only from the footer (site-footer.tsx:78, 95) and the phone Menu (panels.tsx:84). P4-T1 desktop went through Help; P6-T1 needed site search ("autism"). Strategy 4.2 and BR-18: assistance in the header, one interaction from any page.
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Large in-app text clips content and adds sideways scrolling at 320 px
findings.acceptance: At 320 px width with in-app text 112% and 125% (light, dark, high contrast), document scrollWidth equals clientWidth on the 15 key pages including /en/kul/transport and /en/help, and no text is clipped (cards and badges wrap; provenance tags wrap or truncate with a full accessible name); the e2e reflow check covers 320 px at 125%.
findings.evidence: 320x640 at 125% text: home network cards clip 34-55 px (IATA badges cut off), the header "Choose airport" label spills out of its button, /en/kul/transport scrolls 30 px and /en/help 15 px sideways (accessibility-08). 320x568 at 125% text with high contrast: transport scrollWidth 350 px against 320 px; the overflowing elements are provenance tags with shrink-0 and whitespace-nowrap (first-time-access-08).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations
handoffs: C: confirm transport-planner.tsx has no fixed widths once the tag wraps.

findings.title: Overlapping controls on the home first screen
findings.acceptance: Journey mode drives the search direction (Departing gives departures; Arriving and Meeting give arrivals) with at most a small "Search departures instead" link; the airport chooser appears once on the home first screen; no two adjacent controls or cards share a label.
findings.evidence: "Departures | Arrivals" (search scope) sits directly above "Departing | Arriving | Transiting | Meeting someone" (journey mode), and choosing Arriving or Meeting also flips the scope (usability-14). "Choose airport" appears in the header and again in the search card; desktop shows a "Getting to the airport" tile and a same-named card in the notice row (ux-frequent-19).
findings.severity_basis: raised from low: found independently by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Arriving mode does not add the entry checklist (MDAC) to the home
findings.acceptance: In Arriving mode the home shows a "Before you land" card (MDAC within three days, free on the official portal) read from the guide record with its source and as-of date and a link to the Arriving guide, in both languages; no fact is copied into interface strings.
findings.evidence: With Arriving selected the home h2s are Operational notice, Arrivals, Your journey step by step, One network 39 airports, Find something good, Ask in your own words; "Malaysia Digital Arrival Card" appears nowhere (string search), although the rule exists in the Arriving guide and on arrival flight pages.

findings.title: Viewport prefetching costs 40 to 125 KB per mobile load and 235 KB on the desktop board
findings.acceptance: Prefetch only on likely next steps (board, flight, journey); prefetch={false} on footer, mega-menu and long lists, or prefetch on hover/touchstart; no prefetch when navigator.connection.saveData is true or effectiveType is 2g or 3g; at most 5 RSC prefetches per mobile load on the 15 measured pages and under 60 KB of prefetch on the desktop board.
findings.evidence: 8 to 24 RSC prefetches per mobile page load (40 KB on journey to 125 KB on /en/kul) plus the linked routes' JavaScript (transferred JS 322-426 KB against 250-275 KB first-load); desktop /en 25 prefetches (159 KB), /en/kul/flights 39 prefetches (235 KB) and 35 script files. These requests push 11 of 15 pages over the 40-request budget.

findings.title: The KLIA overview buries the operational notice and leads its board preview with gate-closed flights
findings.acceptance: Active operational notices render directly under the airport header on /<lang>/<airport> (inside the first 664 px on a phone); board previews start at now + 15 minutes and exclude departed and gate-closed flights (unit test on the preview filter).
findings.evidence: Phone 390: the Aerotrain night-closure notice is at 2,270 px on /en/kul although the network home shows it near the top. Desktop: the "Departures" preview lists 6 flights, 4 of them "Gate closed". BR-08 asks for the notice on the KLIA homepage and affected pages.

findings.title: One destination, many labels (transport, shop and dine, lounges, facilities)
findings.acceptance: A glossary fixes one noun per section (for example Transport, Parking, Shops and food, Lounges, Facilities, Terminal map) used by tiles, section tabs, page titles and navigation in both languages, with verbs only in tile subtitles; a unit test fails when nav, tab and page-title labels for a section differ.
findings.evidence: Counted in en.ts and features/*.ts: transport has "Getting to the airport", "Getting to and from", "Transport & parking", "Leaving the airport", "Getting to {airport}", "Getting to the terminal"; shop and dine has three variants, lounges four, facilities three. In P2-T1 the tile "Getting to the airport" was the decision point for an arriving visitor.
handoffs: C: align page titles in src/lib/i18n/features/transport.ts, commerce.ts and map.ts with the glossary.
D: align src/lib/i18n/features/guides.ts.

findings.title: Focus ring invisible on the yellow demo banner in dark themes (WCAG 1.4.11)
findings.acceptance: The focus indicator on the banner link is at least 3:1 against the banner in all four themes (for example --color-focus overridden inside the banner).
findings.evidence: Outline #ff9fdc on banner #ffc233 = 1.16:1 (dark) and #ffc2e9 on #ffc233 = 1.09:1 (dark high contrast); light 4.29:1, light HC 5.87:1 (src/app/globals.css:331, 391, 510).

findings.title: Single-key "/" shortcut cannot be turned off (WCAG 2.1.4)
findings.acceptance: Pressing "/" outside a text field no longer opens search unless single-key shortcuts are switched on; Ctrl/Cmd+K still works. Preferred fix: remove "/" (no storage change). A settings switch needs a field in src/lib/preferences.ts, owned by package E.
findings.evidence: With focus on body or a link, "/" opens the Search dialog (src/components/shell/global-overlays.tsx:41); Display settings offer theme, text size, high contrast and reduce motion only.

findings.title: English citation titles on Malay pages lack lang="en"; the translation notice never shows (WCAG 3.1.2)
findings.acceptance: SourceNote wraps source title and publisher in lang="en" unless a Malay title exists; a page with any English citation shows the translation notice once (or a per-citation "EN" marker); a crawl of all /ms pages finds 0 English citation blocks without a lang override.
findings.evidence: 77 of 123 Malay pages show English source titles inside lang="ms" (the Annual Report title on 23 pages; the KLIA Ekspres fare article on /ms/kul and /ms/notices); only 2 blocks on all Malay pages carry lang="en"; the TranslationNotice rendered on 0 Malay pages (content-integrity-10). Measured on /ms/kul/parking (6 titles) and /ms/guides/departing (1) (accessibility-12).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Malay wording to review: "pelepasan", untranslated "Lounge", three names for the concierge
findings.acceptance: Shell and home Malay copy updated to everyday terms (for example "Mencari penerbangan berlepas di 21 lapangan terbang", "Ruang menunggu (lounge) dan hotel"); one concierge term used in ms.ts and features/concierge.ts; i18n test asserts the single term. Final sign-off by a native editor is OOS-14.
findings.evidence: Home helper "Mencari pelepasan di 21 lapangan terbang" ("pelepasan" reads as release or discharge); airport tab "Lounge dan hotel" (first-time-access-16). "Konsierj", "Concierge" and "Tanya concierge" all appear (src/lib/i18n/ms.ts lines 163, 438, 450) (docs-09). The accessibility statement says the Malay is a draft awaiting a native editor.
findings.severity_basis: raised from low: found independently by 2 evaluations
handoffs: B: use the chosen concierge term in src/lib/i18n/features/concierge.ts.

findings.title: The 39-airport chooser interrupts five tasks and does not pin KLIA
findings.acceptance: On /<lang>/airports, KLIA Terminal 1, KLIA Terminal 2 and the last-used airport are large buttons above the filters, inside the first phone screen.
findings.evidence: With no airport chosen every home tile and primary nav item goes to /airports (P1-T2, P2-T1, P3-T1, P7-T1, P9-T2); on the phone the KLIA links sit at about 1,643-1,767 px below the search, state and type filters, while the home's own dialog lists KLIA T1 and T2 first.

findings.title: Home flight-preview links are 26 px tall (product goal 44 px)
findings.acceptance: Each home preview row is a single link at least 44 px tall at 360 px and 125% text; no target in the preview or terminal shortcuts is under 44 px.
findings.evidence: 360 px at 125% text: 20 visible targets under 44 px on the home; destination links in the flight preview are 26 px tall, terminal shortcuts 30-34 px. They pass WCAG 2.5.8 (24 px) but not BR-17 (44 px).

findings.title: Grammar and wording errors in demo, concierge and parking copy
findings.acceptance: The demo note reads "These flights are simulated. Do not use them to plan travel." in both languages; the other three strings are fixed by their owners (hand-offs) and a copy re-read of the four surfaces finds no grammatical errors.
findings.evidence: "These are demonstration flights. Do not use it to plan travel." (flight-search-box.tsx:285 joins flights.search.demoNote and demo.doNotPlan); concierge: "our sources list train between Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 and free shuttle bus between the terminals." (features/concierge.ts:153); parking calculator uses "Arrival date"/"Departure date" for car-park entry and exit; "Calm Room" beside "Calm Room (Terminal 2)".
handoffs: B: rewrite the transfer template in src/lib/i18n/features/concierge.ts with articles.
C: "Entry"/"Exit" labels in src/lib/i18n/features/transport.ts (parking calculator).
D: rename to "Calm Room (Terminal 1)" in src/content/airports/kul.ts.

findings.title: Home shop and dine filters are lost after choosing an airport
findings.acceptance: Chosen filters are carried as query parameters into /<airport>/shop-dine and applied there; filters that cannot return results are hidden (coordinated with the C retail item).
findings.evidence: Filters ticked on the home Shop & dine block are dropped when the visitor then chooses an airport (sitemap.md F4).

findings.title: Breadcrumb structured data helper is unused
findings.acceptance: Every page that renders Breadcrumbs emits a matching BreadcrumbList JSON-LD through the existing helper; a test validates /en/kul/parking.
findings.evidence: src/lib/seo/schemas.ts:89-98 builds a BreadcrumbList matching the visible Breadcrumbs, but no page emits it (sitemap.md F8).

findings.title: The lang cookie is set without Secure
findings.acceptance: The cookie carries Secure when location.protocol is https: (and the __Host- prefix if E updates src/proxy.ts to read the new name).
findings.evidence: language-switch.tsx sets "lang=<lang>; path=/; max-age=31536000; samesite=lax" without Secure; it is the site's only cookie.
handoffs: E: read the renamed cookie in src/proxy.ts if the __Host- prefix is adopted.

packages.name: Flights, journey and concierge
packages.scope: Flight board and flight pages, journey timeline and My journey, flight and operations providers, time utilities, concierge understanding and answers.

findings.title: No operational status layer or queue times (Aerotrain, inter-terminal link, immigration); notices need a deploy
findings.acceptance: In this round: a status-line component (Aerotrain, inter-terminal train, shuttle, immigration) shows state, time and source, fed by current notices until a live feed exists, and says "No disruption reported in our sources as of hh:mm; check the signs" when none applies; it appears in the C-gate and immigration steps of flight timelines and is provided to the home notice strip and KLIA overview (A) and transit (C); demo-labelled security and immigration waits from DemoWaitTimeProvider appear on the flight page and airport overview; tests cover active, upcoming and no-notice states. Live feeds and a CMS with approvals are OOS-02.
findings.evidence: Nothing on the home, notices, transit or map says whether the Aerotrain, train or shuttle runs now; only a planned-closure notice exists and the transit page states a 10 versus 15 minute shuttle conflict (usability-11). /api/health reports a demo waitTimes provider but no page renders waits; the departing timeline says "allow at least 45 minutes" as static text; notices are TypeScript compiled at build time and architecture.md states "no database and no CMS" (exec-commerce-04, docs-14). BR-08, BR-09; ux-frequent Q10 lists checkpoint queue times as must-have with MAHB data.
findings.severity_basis: raised from high: found independently by 3 evaluations
handoffs: A: render the status line in src/components/home/notice-strip.tsx and src/app/[lang]/[airport]/page.tsx.
C: render it in src/components/guides/transit-planner.tsx.

findings.title: Journey timeline marks the wrong step as "Now": check-in after it closed, boarding on a departed flight
findings.acceptance: Timed steps carry an end (check-in closes, gate closes, actual departure or arrival) and the state is computed from start, end and flight status; after check-in closes the timeline says "Check-in has closed: contact <airline>" (or moves on if the passenger has checked in); departed, landed and cancelled flights show a terminal state and no step tells the passenger to go anywhere; journey.test.ts covers check-in close + 1 min, boarding, departure + 1 min, landed and cancelled for departing and arriving journeys.
findings.evidence: At 18:10 MYT MH 2626 shows "Departed, actual 12:00" while its timeline says "Now: 11:15 Board from 11:15 ... be at the gate" (usability-04). At 18:52 MH 2630 reads "Check-in closed" (closed 18:40) but the timeline says "Now: 16:40 Check in and drop your bags"; departed AK 6336 shows "Now: 06:30 Board from 06:30" (ux-frequent-01). Cause: finalise() in src/lib/journey/index.ts (lines 174-186) marks the last step whose start time has passed as current; steps have no end and the flight status is ignored.
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, high; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: The phone flight page does not answer first: status under the bottom bar at 125% text and arrive-by on the eighth screen
findings.acceptance: A summary line under the h1 or in the status panel states the next action and time (for example "Be at KLIA T1 by 19:30 (estimate) · Check in Row H · Boarding 21:45") and links to the timeline step; with the compact chrome in place it is inside the first viewport at 360x780 at 100% and 125% text in both languages; an optional "leave home by" uses the chosen transport mode's published journey time when one is chosen; e2e asserts its position.
findings.evidence: 360x780, Malay, 125% text: page 13,303 px; h1 "MH 2072 ke London" at 724 px, under the fixed bottom bar; status heading 1,267 px; "Tiba di lapangan terbang sebelum 19:30" 6,010 px; gate 7,961 px; no "leave home by" (first-time-access-03). English at 100%: arrive-by step at 3,448 px on the phone and 2,324 px on desktop; the status panel shows times, terminal and gate but not arrive-by (usability-10). ux-frequent measured the gate at 1,306 px; exec measured the desktop status card at 634 px.
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, high; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Flight alerts work only while the page is open, fail silently on iPhone Safari, offer no e-mail and sit eight phone screens down
findings.acceptance: In this round: one "Follow this flight" control sits next to Save in the status card; where the Notification API is missing (including iOS Safari outside an installed web app) it offers e-mail follow and add-to-home-screen guidance instead of a dead end; the e-mail opt-in UI and a FollowChannel provider interface exist with a labelled demo implementation; the copy states exactly what is delivered today. Delivery to a closed browser by push and e-mail is OOS-10.
findings.evidence: On-page copy: "They only arrive while this page is open." With window.Notification absent (iOS Safari outside an installed web app) the panel says "This browser cannot show notifications." and offers nothing else; there is no e-mail or WhatsApp opt-in; the Flight alerts heading is at 5,321 px on a 390 px phone (Save at 1,547 px) (exec-commerce-13, ux-frequent-03). BR-04 is a Must.
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, high; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Board rows and flight-detail values (gate, belt, counters) appear with no demonstration label in view
findings.acceptance: Using the compact demo tag from package A, every board time-group header (or every row at narrow widths) and the gate, belt and counter values in the status hero carry a demo marker; the in-view measurement reports 100% of rows and values labelled at 390x844 and 1280x900 on /en/kul/flights, /ms/kul/flights, /en/pen/flights and two flight pages; the check runs in CI.
findings.evidence: /en/kul/flights: 47 of 53 rows have no demo label in view on desktop and 52 of 53 on the phone (the same on /ms; Penang 7 of 12 and 11 of 12); the only label is the non-sticky banner above the board; a phone screenshot shows MH 1662 Shanghai, Gate C35, "Boarding" with no label on screen (content-integrity-01). Flight detail on the phone: "CHECK-IN Row X · Counters 5-10", "GATE K15" and "BAGGAGE BELT 2" with no label in view; banner at y=550, gate at y=1252 (content-integrity-03). Build spec rule 1.

findings.title: Demo flight generation runs on the main thread during render and on every board keystroke (INP 736 to 832 ms)
findings.acceptance: Every board keystroke and the journey direction switch respond within 200 ms on a 4x-throttled Pixel 7 profile (Event Timing, 3 runs); the filtered list derives from useDeferredValue or a transition; the two-day search pool is computed once per provider instant and cached per airport and date across provider instances; timezone offsets are computed once per day (no formatToParts per flight); rendered rows are capped (for example 40 with "Show more"); providers.test.ts and time.test.ts cover the cache.
findings.evidence: Pixel 7 emulation at 4x CPU, typing "MH" in the board filter: worst interaction 784, 832 and 736 ms; long animation frame 729 ms with 523 ms of script in the input handler; clearing the filter 304-328 ms. CPU profile: 1,048 ms busy, zonedParts (Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatToParts) 296 ms, 262 rows rendered at once. The same zonedParts cost (653 ms) dominates home hydration; getFlightProvider creates a new provider every 30 s and the direction flip regenerates the pool.

findings.title: My journey shows a skeleton until hydration, then swaps it: CLS 0.11 to 0.23 and LCP 5.3 to 5.6 s on slow 4G
findings.acceptance: The server HTML of /en/journey contains the empty state; saved flights replace it after storage is read with CLS at or under 0.05 on mobile and desktop (2 loads each); LCP at or under 2.5 s on applied slow 4G; MyJourney receives only the notes and sources its saved flights need.
findings.evidence: Applied slow-4G Lighthouse: performance 46/50, LCP 5.6/5.3 s (element: the empty-state paragraph), CLS 0.211 (footer). Playwright CLS 0.2265 mobile and 0.1136 desktop in 2 of 2 loads. MyJourney returns a skeleton while !hydrated, then the empty state or saved flight at a different height; the page passes 33 KB of notes and 19 KB of sources to the client component.

findings.title: Concierge misses direct answers: fares, airline terminal, nearest lounge, Fast Track, duty free, Aerotrain status, accessible qualifiers, autogates, "how early"
findings.acceptance: Slot-specific intents in both languages whose first statement is the direct answer with its source: fare for a named mode (with the dated fare change), airline to terminal at KLIA (from the airline records; "confirm on your booking" where unverified), lounge nearest a gate ranked by flight context, Fast Track, duty free, Aerotrain and inter-terminal status (reads current notices), immigration and autogates, and "how early" (3 h international, 2 h domestic, then offer flight lookup). Qualifiers "accessible", "step-free" and "elderly/warga emas" filter statements to step-free fields and fall back to an explicit "not published, ask ..." answer. Every question quoted in the five source findings is in engine.test.ts and the BR-20 evaluation set, with the expected intent and first statement.
findings.evidence: POST /api/concierge: "How much is the KLIA Ekspres?" and "Berapa tambang KLIA Ekspres?" lead with shuttle FAQs and bury RM 55; "Which terminal does Emirates/AirAsia use?" gets "check your booking" or "I could not match that to one topic"; "lounge near gate G6 in business class" lists all 5 T1 lounges unranked (ux-frequent-11, usability-13, docs-03). "Can I buy fast track at KLIA?" and "Where can I buy duty free chocolate?" return intent unknown, and "Is there fast track at KLIA?" leads with the Butterfly Effect hidden-disability programme; "Is the Aerotrain running?" maps to the gates intent (exec-commerce-17). "Where do I get an accessible taxi?" and "step-free access to KLIA Ekspres" get a generic transport list; "Boleh ibu saya guna autogate?" is unknown; "Pukul berapa perlu sampai?" asks for a flight number instead of giving the 3-hour guidance (first-time-access-09).
findings.severity_basis: raised from medium: found independently by 5 evaluations

findings.title: No feed-failure or last-known-data state; flights are generated in the browser and the official provider is a stub
findings.acceptance: Flights are served from the server through the provider interface with a cache (which also removes the generator from client bundles); the board, flight page and (via A) home search show last-known data with its age within 2 s of a failure, offer retry, and no spinner lasts more than 10 s; a chaos test (provider throws, times out, returns stale data) and a contract test against the official provider interface run in CI. Connecting the official feed is OOS-01.
findings.evidence: src/lib/providers/official-flights.ts line 96: "Stub that documents the live integration. Every data method throws ProviderNotConfiguredError." PROVIDER_MODES sets flights, waitTimes and parkingAvailability to demo (src/lib/providers/index.ts). No last-known, stale, retry or error state exists in src/components/flights outside the alerts panel; flights are generated in the browser during hydration, so no network failure can occur today and none is handled. BR-05.
handoffs: A: stale and failed states in src/components/flights/flight-search-box.tsx.
E: /api/flights serves the cached provider data with the new limits.

findings.title: Delayed and cancelled board times rely on strikethrough to show which time is old (WCAG 1.3.1)
findings.acceptance: Delayed and cancelled times expose "Scheduled 17:25, now 18:20" and "Cancelled, was 17:25" to assistive technology on the board table, phone list and saved-flight card, reusing the flight page's Scheduled/Estimated strings; an accessibility-tree snapshot test covers both.
findings.evidence: The time cell for a delayed flight is 17:25 18:20, exposed as "17:25 18:20" with no "scheduled" or "estimated" word; most screen readers do not announce . Same pattern in the phone list and saved-flight card (flight-row.tsx:83, 136; saved-flight-card.tsx:103). The flight detail page is correct.

findings.title: Assistance needs can never be set, so no timeline shows the assistance step
findings.acceptance: A "My needs" control (wheelchair, step-free, older traveller, travelling with someone who needs help) stored on the device without an account (new src/lib/needs.ts using the existing createStore) is offered on the flight page and My journey and passed to buildJourney by both callers; with a need set, departing and arriving timelines include the assistance step with the operating airline's lead time and the airport service, and map links use sf=1; journey.test.ts and an e2e test cover it.
findings.evidence: JourneyPreferences.reducedMobility (src/lib/journey/index.ts:35) adds assistanceStep() for departing (line 392) and arriving (line 604) journeys, but both callers (journey-timeline.tsx:63, my-journey.tsx:75) call buildJourney without preferences, and no control anywhere asks about needs; MH 2072 (8 steps) and MH 2073 (6 steps) show no assistance step. BR-18.
handoffs: D: render the needs control on /accessibility (src/app/[lang]/accessibility/page.tsx).

findings.title: The status card gives one cabin's check-in row as the flight's, and contradicts the timeline
findings.acceptance: checkInRow is modelled per cabin, plus bag drop, in the flight type; the card shows up to three short lines ("Economy: Row H 1-18 · Business: Row D 4-12 · Bag drop: F, G") or labels the cabin when only one is known; with no feed row it falls back to the airline's published rows with provenance; a unit test over demo flights with and without feed rows proves card and timeline agree.
findings.evidence: MH 2630 card: "CHECK-IN Row H · Counters 1-18"; the timeline note says Row H is international Economy, Row D (counters 4-12) Business, bag drop F and G; a business traveller following the card goes to the wrong row (flight-status-hero.tsx:51-52, demo provider field) (ux-frequent-08). MH 2072 card: "CHECK-IN Shown nearer the time" while the timeline and airline card give Row H (first-time-access-18).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Flight-page links lose the flight's context, and the timeline ignores gate, cabin and dwell time
findings.acceptance: Contextual links carry what the destination can use: shop-dine ?gate=<terminal>-<gate>&t=<terminal>, parking ?t=<terminal>&from=<ISO>&to=<ISO>, transport ?t=; the "time to spare" step lists the nearest lounge and outlets to the gate on the passenger's side of security; two remembered toggles ("Hand luggage only", "Business or lounge access") adjust arrive-by from sourced airline deadlines (Estimated where unsourced); an optional, non-preselected Fast Track action follows the security step on departing flights; journey.test.ts covers the parameters.
findings.evidence: For MH 570 at gate C27, "Find the gate on the map" passes gate and terminal but "Browse food and shops" links /en/kul/shop-dine and "See parking" /en/kul/parking with no terminal or dates (src/lib/journey/index.ts lines 287 and 504); no lounge suggestion (exec-commerce-07). "Arrive at the airport by 16:40: 3 hours before your international flight" for a 65-minute KUL-SIN hop; no hand-luggage, cabin or Fast Track options; Plaza Premium Lounge near gate G is not suggested for gate G6; security plus immigration is a flat 45 minutes (ux-frequent-13).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Flight ids: codeshare URLs return "not found"; unknown ids are rendered per request at full cost
findings.acceptance: A codeshare id redirects (308) to the operating flight's page for that date and airport; ids that fail the id shape (src/lib/flights/id.ts) or are unknown return 404 through notFound() with a small body (under 30 KB) before flight data is built; valid ids are cacheable for a short time (s-maxage at most 60 s); tests cover codeshare, malformed and unknown ids; security.md section 1 is updated through E.
findings.evidence: Home search resolves "QR5700" to MH 2630, but /en/kul/flights/qr5700-20261118-d renders "We could not find this flight" (ux-frequent-09). Unknown ids (zz9999-20990101-d, an encoded tag, a 1,600-character string) all return 200, about 450 KB, Cache-Control no-store; 40 concurrent random ids took 1.4-4.2 s against 7 ms for the prerendered board; no rate limit applies (security-05).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations
findings.priority_reason: on the security evaluator's fix-before-production list

findings.title: Concierge: the skeleton-then-consent swap shifts the page, and consent interrupts a tapped suggested question
findings.acceptance: The consent text and question field are in the server HTML (CLS at or under 0.05 on /en/concierge, mobile); deterministic answers to suggested questions appear immediately with the privacy notice inline above the answer, and consent is asked only before AI wording or saved-flight use; the concierge is offered from the phone Search sheet (A hand-off).
findings.evidence: Pixel 7: layout shift 0.14 at 349-399 ms when the consent panel replaces the role=status skeleton; the question field does not exist until hydration (performance-12). Tapping "How do I get from Terminal 1 to Terminal 2?" opens "Before you ask" and answers only after "Agree and start"; on the phone the suggestions are about 6,600 px down the home and the bottom bar has no concierge entry (usability-21).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations
handoffs: A: add a concierge entry to the phone Search sheet (src/components/search/command-palette.tsx or src/components/shell/mobile-bar.tsx).

findings.title: Boards open 45 minutes in the past, so departed flights lead
findings.acceptance: Boards open at now minus at most 10 minutes, or keep 45 minutes but scroll to and visually collapse departed rows behind "Show earlier flights"; on /en/kul/flights at 390 px the first row shown has not departed; board-model.test.ts covers the window.
findings.evidence: Phone 390 at about 18:55: header "17:53 to 00:38"; the first row (AK 6340, Departed) is at 1,173 px and 5 of the first 8 rows have departed; the first flight still to depart is at 1,298 px and the 18:55 departures start at about 2,478 px. board-model.ts:132 sets back = 45 minutes.

findings.title: Greeter view leads with long-stay parking and gives no pick-up point
findings.acceptance: For the meeting kind, steps lead with where to wait and pick up (arrival hall level, e-hailing pick-up area and entry fee with date or "Not published", kerb rules) and short-stay parking ("See parking" with a 3-hour preset); long-stay warnings are not shown to greeters; journey.test.ts covers the meeting kind.
findings.evidence: P9-T1 (Meeting someone, MH 2088 arrival): steps start with "Decide where to park or wait", followed by "Parking for a longer trip" and "Avoid Preferred Parking" (RM2,084 bill); exit estimate and "Wait in the arrival hall" (Level 3) are good; no pick-up point, e-hailing pick-up area or entry fee, only "Do not wait at the kerb".
handoffs: D: add sourced pick-up point and e-hailing entry-fee notes for the meeting topic in src/content/airports/kul.ts.

findings.title: Live board auto-updates every 30 seconds with no pause control (WCAG 2.2.2)
findings.acceptance: A "Pause live updates" control beside "Refreshes every 30 seconds" stops and resumes refresh; updates also pause while a row has focus or hover; the state change is announced politely.
findings.evidence: 80 s recording with a flight link focused: rows dropped from 63 to 61 and "Updated" changed; focus stayed and the page scrolled 90 px to keep it; no control to pause or slow updates (demo-flights.ts:44, use-flight-provider.ts:17).

findings.title: Board changes are never announced, even for a saved flight
findings.acceptance: On refresh, a status, gate or time change to a saved flight posts one polite live-region message; unchanged refreshes post nothing.
findings.evidence: Over 80 s the only live-region change was the aria-live=off timestamp; the build spec asks for polite board-update announcements.

findings.title: Concierge question field drops below the fold after an answer while keeping focus
findings.acceptance: After each answer at 1280x800 and 390x844 the focused question field stays in the viewport (sticky composer or scrollIntoView with block "nearest").
findings.evidence: 1280x800: after one answer the focused field moved from y=534 to y=1027, outside the viewport.

findings.title: Flight-number h1 in old-style figures; the route is stated three times
findings.acceptance: Flight numbers use lining, tabular figures (or the sans) wherever shown; the route is stated once above the status card.
findings.evidence: Screenshots at 390, 360 and 1280: "MH 2630 to Singapore" in the display serif with old-style figures (the 3 descends); the lead "Malaysia Airlines. Kuala Lumpur (KUL) to Singapore (SIN)." and the card header repeat the route.

packages.name: Airport sections: map, facilities, transport, parking, transit, lounges, shop and dine
packages.scope: Every airport section page except flights and the overview, their components and logic, the transit planner and the shared section-page helper.

findings.title: Parking is not price-first, the Terminal 1 car park has no price, and the booking hand-off carries no dates
findings.acceptance: In this round: the page leads with a compact matrix (car park x 1 day / 3 days / 7 days) inside the first phone viewport once the compact chrome lands; "Not verified" cells show the dated conflicting source figures as a range with sources and link out; the Preferred Parking warning moves into its row; the booking link carries product and entry/exit dates where the official site accepts them, otherwise the dates are shown beside the link; e2e covers the matrix position. Running the calculator on the official tariff and a dated, attributed booking deep link are OOS-03.
findings.evidence: All 4 KLIA car parks show "Rates: Not verified"; "3 days" gives "At most RM 96" for the Long Term Car Park only; Terminal 1 Car Park for 3 hours: "No estimate ... an undated Malaysia Airports page gives RM4 an hour for the first three hours and klia.info gives a daily maximum of RM52" (exec-commerce-02, usability-19). Phone: after the h1 come a Book link and two callouts; the "3 days" chip is at 2,029 px and the estimate at 2,206 px; 1,348 words and 17 not-verified mentions (ux-frequent-14). "Book parking online" opens the official page with no product, dates or referral. BR-10.
findings.severity_basis: raised from high: found independently by 3 evaluations

findings.title: No anti-touting or official-taxi guidance at the transport decision; no rail ticket links
findings.acceptance: Arrival-side transport views show, at the top and beside taxi and e-hailing cards, "Book taxis only at the coupon counters; ignore anyone offering a ride", reusing the guide statement and its sources and linking to the Help scam answer; the coupon taxi with its counters is listed for every city destination; each mode with an official ticket channel links to it (official channels only); e2e checks /en/kul/transport and /ms/kul/transport.
findings.evidence: /en/kul/transport?t=T1 contains no "tout", "scam", "unofficial" or "offering a ride"; with the default destination KL Sentral the coupon taxi appears only under "Not listed for KL Sentral" and its counters and fares only after changing destination (usability-01). KLIA Ekspres fares are dated but "check kliaekspres.com" is plain text with no ticket link; the anti-touting statement exists in the arriving guide (src/content/guides.ts line 211) and Help but not on the comparison (exec-commerce-16). BR-11.
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, high; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: The self-transfer verdict is 2,943 to 4,279 px down the phone page, after the steps
findings.acceptance: A verdict card (verdict word, one sentence, time range, "If it is tight" action) renders directly below the form and before the steps on phone and desktop; at 390x664 it is within one screen of the form's last control; verdict changes are announced politely; e2e asserts the order.
findings.evidence: With the usability inputs, "Tight. Your time sits inside our estimate..." at 4,279 px on the phone (2,652 px on desktop) after eleven steps; P7-T1 took 6 interactions against a target of 3 (usability-07). With default inputs, "Looks workable" at 2,943 px on a 10,336 px page (ux-frequent-12).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, high; found by 2 evaluations
handoffs: D: add any new verdict-card strings under guidePages.transit in src/lib/i18n/features/guides.ts.

findings.title: The map gives an illustrative prayer-room pin a level and area that the directory says are unpublished
findings.acceptance: For demo-provenance map points linked to a facility whose location is unpublished, the panel shows "Position illustrative: level and area not published" instead of Level and Area (or "Show on map" is not rendered); map-logic.test.ts covers it.
findings.evidence: Facilities card "Prayer rooms (surau)": "Locations and levels are not yet verified ... Not published: Location, Level, Area, Opening hours and Accessibility", with a "Show on map" link; the map panel then states "Level 5: departures. Area: Public area (landside)" from a point with provenance "demo" (src/content/airports/kul.ts).
handoffs: D: add a content.test.ts rule that a map point cannot assert fields its facility lacks.

findings.title: Retail discovery dead-ends: filters return nothing; no hours, images, reserve-and-collect or offers
findings.acceptance: In this round: filters that cannot return results with current data are hidden or disabled with a reason on /<airport>/shop-dine and on the home strip (A hand-off); no offered filter returns "0 of 8". Hours, price bands, images, reserve-and-collect and an offer slot are OOS-05.
findings.evidence: The home strip offers "Open now", "Halal", "Before security", "After security"; /en/kul/shop-dine?filters=open-now shows "0 of 8. Outlets without published hours are left out"; hours 0 of 8, price bands 0 of 8, no outlet images; Eraman duty-free outlets have no pre-order link; no labelled offer slot exists. ux-frequent Q10 lists outlet hours as must-have with MAHB data.
handoffs: A: hide the same filters in src/components/home/shop-dine-strip.tsx.

findings.title: Missing airport sections: 404 under a section title, 200 on the first request, and indexable empty map and transit pages
findings.acceptance: airportSectionMetadata returns the not-found title and noindex when the airport lacks the section; section routes export dynamicParams = false (or reject unknown airport-section pairs before rendering) so every request for a missing section is 404 from the first request; map and transit empty-state variants are 404 or noindex; a curl test over 39 airports x 9 sections checks the first and a repeat request.
findings.evidence: /en/szb/parking returns 404 "Page not found" with the title "Parking at Subang | Malaysia Airports" because airportSectionMetadata builds the title before section availability is checked (usability-25; src/components/airport/section-page.ts). The first requests to /en/kch/parking, /en/lgk/transport, /en/bki/shop-dine, /en/lgk/parking and /en/pen/shop-dine return 200 with not-found content, later 404 (exec-commerce-18). /{airport}/map and /{airport}/transit answer for all 39 airports as unlinked empty states (docs-06).
findings.severity_basis: raised from low: found independently by 3 evaluations

findings.title: Nursing rooms are absent from Facilities with no "not published" placeholder
findings.acceptance: Facilities shows placeholder cards for expected but unverified categories (nursing room, accessible toilet) with "Not published" and the information-counter route, mirroring the map's list; a parent reaches the nursing-room answer from Facilities in 2 interactions.
findings.evidence: P3-T1: 17 facilities at T1, none about nursing or baby care, although "nursing-room" is a defined category; the only answer is in the Families guide, reached by site search after a dead end; the map lists "Not on this map yet: Accessible toilets, Nursing rooms".

findings.title: Step-free arrival route omits the lift and immigration, has a vague "Walk on" step and stops short of the taxi
findings.acceptance: Step-free routes emit a named "change level" step with the lift for every level transition, include immigration and customs as named steps, and can end at the taxi counter, rail entrance or e-hailing pick-up once D adds those places; map-logic.test.ts covers gate C to taxi counter.
findings.evidence: Gate C to arrivals pick-up, sf=1: "About 760 m, 14 min / 19 min"; steps 4 "Walk on" 70 m and 5 "Continue through to Level 3: arrivals" 200 m name no lift and no immigration, although the map has "Arrival immigration" and lift places; taxi coupon counters are not a map place.
handoffs: D: add taxi counter, rail entrance and e-hailing pick-up as map places in src/content/airports/kul.ts.

findings.title: Duplicate option names in the map route From and To lists
findings.acceptance: Every option label is unique per terminal (full place name or building appended); a unit test asserts uniqueness.
findings.evidence: The From and To selects (40 options each) contain "Aerotrain station · Gates" twice and "Malaysia Airlines Golden Lounge · Gates" three times; the qualifiers exist in the place names but are dropped in the option text.

findings.title: Transport page: an h3 precedes its section h2 in source order (WCAG 1.3.1)
findings.acceptance: The section heading comes first in source order (visual order via CSS grid if needed); heading-order check passes on /en/kul/transport.
findings.evidence: In the region "Not covered here yet", h3 "Driving yourself" comes before h2 "Not covered here yet" in the DOM (both at y=3036).

findings.title: Lounges and day rooms are listed but cannot be priced or booked
findings.acceptance: When operators supply them: access rules, price and a booking action per lounge from the operator, with price and booking fields in the facility model, and a dwell-time suggestion on departing and transit timelines. Until then each card states "Price and access rules not published" once.

findings.title: "Official" tag on facts that rest only on news, blogs, relays or the prototype itself
findings.acceptance: validateContent rejects provenance "official" unless at least one cited source is kind official, government or operator on the authority's own domain, and never accepts prototype-method for it; the 9 records are retagged "estimated" or gain a first-party source (kliaekspres.com fare page, Mavcom notice, MAHB notice); the 8 misclassified sources are reclassified or given the first-party URL; prototype statements carry no Official tag; content.test.ts passes with the rule; the concierge shows the same tag as the page.

Answers about the prototype on /help/about-this-site and /help/privacy carry Official with only prototype-method as source (content-integrity-05). The finding closes only when the related items' Fast Track checks also pass: "fast track" and "laluan pantas" return it first in search (A), the concierge answers from it (B), departing timelines offer it as an optional, non-preselected action after security (B) and the legacy fast-track path redirects to it (E).

packages.name: Platform, performance and security
packages.scope: Root layout and streaming, API routes, proxy and headers, SEO, storage layer, i18n runtime, service worker, concierge server security, CI, budgets, dependencies and engineering docs.
owned_paths: .github/ at the repository root (only the new malaysia-airports CI workflow and Dependabot config; deploy.yml stays untouched)

findings.title: Mobile performance below target on every page (Lighthouse 56 to 92, TBT up to 2 s); budgets not enforced
findings.acceptance: Lighthouse CI on /en, /ms, /en/kul/flights, one flight page and /en/journey (mobile, median of 3) fails the build below performance 95, above TBT 200 ms, CLS 0.1 or LCP 2.5 s, and over byte budgets (home JS 250 KB; guidance pages 500 KB and 40 requests); all 15 measured pages reach performance 95 once the dependent items land.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse 13.6 mobile, median of 3: /en 56, /ms 65, /en/kul 78, board 81, flight detail 64, journey 64, map 68, transport 89, parking 83, shop-dine 67, guides 91, transit 68, concierge 91, corporate 92, airports 81; TBT 338-1,978 ms on every page; simulated TTI 4.3-6.4 s; on the Malaysian median network /en still scores 74 (performance-01). Guidance pages 582-720 KB against a 500 KB budget; 37-64 requests (performance-15). Panels measured home 75-77 (TBT 1,076-1,308 ms) and flight page 66-67 (LCP 4.4-4.8 s) (exec-commerce-19, ux-frequent-17; first-time-access measured /ms 68).
findings.severity_basis: raised from high: found independently by 3 evaluations

findings.title: Root loading.tsx streams every page through a fallback: desktop CLS 0.23 to 0.29 and LCP delayed to 4.1 to 4.8 s
findings.acceptance: The root src/app/[lang]/loading.tsx is removed (fallbacks only on dynamic segments such as the flight detail page); static pages emit the h1 and lead in the first HTML flush with no $RC reveal; desktop CLS at or under 0.1 on /en, /ms, /en/kul and /en/concierge (2 of 2 loads); Lighthouse mobile LCP at or under 2.5 s on the six pages (median of 3) and on the congested Wi-Fi profile for /en and the board.
findings.evidence: 1440x900, 2 of 2 loads: the footer moves from y=640 out of the viewport, CLS 0.2889 on /en, /ms and /en/kul and 0.2317 on /en/concierge; the fallback is inserted at 57-78 ms, segments revealed by $RC at 108-137 ms (performance-04). Lighthouse mobile median LCP 4.1-4.8 s on /en, flight detail, journey, map, shop-dine and transit, because the LCP element is revealed after the whole body with 300 ms reveal batching; congested Wi-Fi /en 2.9 s (performance-07). Every page under [lang] is wrapped by src/app/[lang]/loading.tsx.
handoffs: A: review Suspense fallbacks in src/app/[lang]/[airport]/layout.tsx.

findings.title: Every route ships 250 to 312 KB gzip of first-load JavaScript, 120 KB of it shell code (zod, icon registry, demo generator, Radix)
findings.acceptance: First-load JS at or under 250 KB gzip on /en and at or under 170 KB on content and guidance pages (same measurement as performance-08); no zod classic or content schemas in client chunks (client storage validation uses zod/mini or hand-written guards; stores.ts and preferences.ts import no runtime values from src/content/types.ts); with the hand-offs done, the icon registry tree-shakes, the demo generator is not in the shell, and the search, concierge and switcher dialogs load on first open.
findings.evidence: Build manifest, gzip -9: framework 128.6 KB plus the same eight [lang]/layout chunks 120.1 KB on every route; totals 250.3 (corporate) to 275.3 KB (flight detail), /en 263.0 KB; shell chunks: zod 4 classic plus content schemas 34.1 KB (22-24 KB unused at load), about 145 lucide icons in a name-keyed registry 22.7 KB, the demo flight generator 12.7 KB, Radix 32 KB (performance-08). The earlier documentation review measured 294-312 KB (docs-10). stores.ts imports TERMINAL_IDS from src/content/types.ts, pulling the content schemas into the client.
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, high; found by 2 evaluations
handoffs: A: split the icon registry (src/components/ui/icon.tsx) and lazy-load the search, concierge and airport-switcher dialogs (src/components/shell/global-overlays.tsx).
B: keep the demo generator out of the shell (dynamic import or server side, see the feed-failure item).
D: if TERMINAL_IDS must move, re-export it from a zod-free module in src/content/types.ts.

findings.title: Concierge buffers the whole request body before enforcing the 4 KB limit
findings.acceptance: Content-Length over 4,096 bytes gets 413 before the body is read; bodies without Content-Length are read as a stream with a byte counter and aborted past 4,096 bytes; a 200 MB POST leaves RSS within 10 MB of baseline; server.test.ts covers both.
findings.evidence: A 200,000,000-byte POST returned 413 after 0.68 s, but next-server RSS rose from 212,140 KB to 777,500 KB and stayed there 13 s later; route.ts calls await request.text() and then compares raw.length (UTF-16 units, not bytes) with MAX_BODY_BYTES = 4096 (src/app/api/concierge/route.ts lines 25-38).

findings.title: Concierge rate limit keys on a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For: bypass and victim lockout
findings.acceptance: The key comes from a trusted source (configured trusted proxy hop or CDN client-IP header), never the first X-Forwarded-For entry; invalid requests are counted; the bucket sits behind a shared-store interface; a global per-minute model-call budget with a circuit breaker exists; a test with rotating X-Forwarded-For values gets 429 after 10.
findings.evidence: 14 posts with one X-Forwarded-For: 10 x 200 then 429; 30 posts with rotating values: 30 x 200; 30 invalid posts (400) never counted; clientKey() takes the first X-Forwarded-For entry (src/lib/concierge/rate-limit.ts:56); the bucket is per-process memory. With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set, each allowed request can trigger a paid model call.

findings.title: No CI for the app; the automated security checks security.md promises do not exist; Chromium only; axe tag set incomplete
findings.acceptance: A workflow at the repository root (.github/workflows/malaysia-airports-ci.yml, paths malaysia-airports/**, pull requests and manual runs) runs npm ci, next typegen, tsc, lint, unit tests, build, Playwright desktop and phone (plus a WebKit phone project if the browser is available, otherwise documented), axe through a shared e2e/support/axe.ts exporting wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa, npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high as a gate, CodeQL and gitleaks over full history; Dependabot or Renovate is configured; the workflow passes on a clean checkout.
findings.evidence: The repository's only workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yml) builds the parent curriculum site: no CI for malaysia-airports, no npm audit gate, no CodeQL or other SAST, no Dependabot or Renovate, no secret scanning (security-08, docs-11). Both Playwright projects use Chromium; WebKit (Safari on iPhone) is not covered (docs-12). The e2e axe scans omit wcag21a (ux-frequent-06, tracked in package A).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations
findings.priority_reason: on the security evaluator's fix-before-production list

findings.title: Any website can make visitors' browsers post to the concierge (no preflight, no origin check)
findings.acceptance: Only the exact application/json media type is accepted; requests with Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site, or an Origin other than the site origin, get 403; the cross-origin no-cors test no longer changes X-RateLimit-Remaining.
findings.evidence: A page on another origin sent four no-cors POSTs with Content-Type "text/plain;x=application/json" and the concierge processed them (X-RateLimit-Remaining 9 to 4); curl with Origin https://evil.example and Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site got 200; the check is includes('application/json') (route.ts:34).
findings.priority_reason: on the security evaluator's fix-before-production list

findings.title: No rate limit on /api/flights, /api/health or dynamic pages, and no edge configuration in the repository
findings.acceptance: Per-route limits for /api/flights, /api/health and dynamic pages are defined as code (proxy or route middleware behind a shared-store interface) and tested (a 300-request burst gets 429 after the limit); edge rules (per-route buckets, bot scoring, body limits) are written as configuration for the chosen host. Deploying them on MAHB infrastructure is OOS-11.
findings.evidence: 300 burst requests to /api/flights?airport=kul: 300 x 200; /api/health and flight detail pages are unlimited too; no WAF, CDN or infrastructure-as-code exists although security.md section 4 puts limits at the edge first.
findings.priority_reason: on the security evaluator's fix-before-production list

findings.title: CSP allows inline script with no reporting; the header policy will block checkout integrations
findings.acceptance: A report-only policy with hashes for the static preferences init script and require-trusted-types-for 'script' reports to a same-origin endpoint; after a clean report window the enforced policy drops 'unsafe-inline' for scripts (nonces on dynamic routes); per-route overrides let a checkout route allow payment=(self) plus a named payment origin and partner frame-src/connect-src without loosening other routes; security-headers.test.ts covers both.
findings.evidence: Every response: script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline', no report-to or Reporting-Endpoints, no Trusted Types; 0 violations observed on 14 routes (security-07). Permissions-Policy includes payment=(); connect-src 'self' and no frame-src (src/lib/seo/security-headers.ts line 71), so checkout and partner widgets cannot work; BR-24 requires no unsafe-inline (exec-commerce-14).
findings.severity_basis: highest source rating, medium; found by 2 evaluations

findings.title: Optional AI wording path: the fact guard passes web addresses, e-mails and anything typed in the question; tags injectable; no spend cap
findings.acceptance: The pilot runs without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY until: the guard rejects any URL, domain, e-mail or phone not present in the retrieved statements; the question is excluded from the grounding reference for names and numbers and sent as its own content block with < and > escaped; max_tokens is about 200; daily and monthly spend caps, a circuit breaker and counters exist; passport, booking, phone and e-mail patterns are redacted; the four red-team cases above are rejected in tests.
findings.evidence: With fake model replies, checkGrounded accepted "Book your parking at klia-parking-deals.example", "Email refunds@scam.example ...", "you do not need a passport ... just walk through security" and, because the question is part of groundingReference(), a phone number typed in the question; "</question><draft>...</draft>" is pasted unescaped into the user message; max_tokens 2048 for 480-character output; no budget, circuit breaker or counters. The path is off unless ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set.

findings.title: The whole interface dictionary (127 KB, 39 KB gzip) is inlined in every page; the flight page sends it twice
findings.acceptance: Each client island receives only its namespace (or server-rendered strings); corporate copy never reaches passenger pages; content-page HTML at or under 40 KB gzip; the flight page carries the dictionary and props once, passing the airport slug and needed fields instead of the airport object (B hand-off).
findings.evidence: I18nProvider in the root layout receives getDictionary(lang): 126,921 bytes of JSON (38,942 gzip) on every page, including 28.7 KB of corporate copy, about half the home's 78 KB gzip HTML; the flight page contains the dictionary twice and its FlightDetail props twice (each with the whole 19 KB airport object): 500 KB raw, 127 KB gzip; /en/journey passes 33 KB of notes and 19 KB of sources.
handoffs: B: pass only needed fields in src/app/[lang]/[airport]/flights/[flightId]/page.tsx and src/app/[lang]/journey/page.tsx.

findings.title: Service-worker install on a first visit makes 94 fetches, downloads /en three times and brings the first visit to 1.07 MB
findings.acceptance: A first visit downloads /en once; the worker precaches only the current language's offline page and shell, dedupes asset fetches and starts after network idle; first visit at or under 600 KB and 60 requests; Cache Storage after install at or under 1 MB; sw-routes.test.ts updated.

findings.title: API hygiene: unbounded date, duplicate parameters accepted, HTML 404 for unknown API paths
